thread:
sanam: FYI I'm seeing a p95 regression on Mistral-8x7B after the kernel-selector change that went out yesterday. Only on long sliding-window workloads (~5-7k tokens). Dashboard: https://perf.redwood/infer/streams/abc123 :thinking:

alex: Can you paste the profiler / kernel selection log for a slow request?

sanam: Pasting snippet from the traces (trimmed):
```
[KERNEL_SELECTOR] chosen: matmul_v2_tile64 (est=0.82ms)
[KERNEL_SELECTOR] fallback: matmul_generic (est=1.4ms)
[KV_CACHE] hit_rate=0.93 ptr_mod=2048 seq=6144 max_pos=4096
[INFER] total_tokens=6144 p95=248ms (prev=190ms)
```
Looks like chosen kernel has worse end-to-end perf when KV pointer arithmetic wraps (seq > max_pos) and we do sliding-window attention.

maria: Could be RoPE scaling mismatch when we normalize positions across the sliding window. If rope_scale is bumped for >max_pos we change the distribution of attention and that can affect kernel runtime behavior too. Did the selector recently add a branch based on "effective_seq_len"?

sanam: Yes — selector now picks kernels using a heuristic that takes (seq_len, kv_stride, head_dim). For effective_seq_len > model.max_position_embeddings we force a different matmul path to optimize cache locality. That seemed ok on synthetic but fails on real workloads.

alex: Quick experiment: try disabling the new branch locally and re-run the canary. Command we used: `KERNEL_SELECTOR_V2=0 ./run_canary --model mistral-8x7b --profile`

tj: I ran that on canary-3 this morning. Results: p95 dropped from 248ms -> 205ms, tail allocations down, KV ptr churn metric reduced by ~18%. So disabling the branch helps.

sanam: Good. I also dumped KV stats and saw pointer oscillation: when sliding window slides by chunk=128, kv_index is doing modulo with kv_capacity=4096 and we end up reusing slots frequently. Patch idea: bias the modulo by a monotonic offset so reused indices are contiguous rather than scattered, which should help matmul kernels that prefer sequential KV layout.

maria: That aligns with a hypothesis where the matmul tile kernel gets pathological page-crossing patterns. If indices jump around, kernel prefetchers lose. Two follow-ups: (1) try the biased-modulo and (2) add a small rope_scale clamp for positions > max_pos to keep the attention distribution stable.

sanam: Prototype biased-modulo (in C-like pseudocode):
```
// offset increases per sliding window step
kv_index = (pos + window_offset) % kv_capacity;
window_offset = (window_offset + chunk) % kv_capacity;
```
I tested locally with microbench and matmul_v2 latency improved 12-15% for long sequences.

alex: Nice. Also add a kernel-selector guard: don't choose matmul_v2_tile64 when kv_index variance > threshold. We can compute variance cheaply per-request.

tj: One more oddity: attention mask generation for sliding windows was tagging positions > max_pos as masked=false in a few cases due to an off-by-one in the wrap logic. That effectively changes the active sequence length passed to kernels. Patch coming.

infra-bot: deploybot: Canary deploy 2026-03-15T10:02 applied to canary-3 (team: eng-runtime).

maria: Good catch on the mask. If mask toggles unexpectedly, the kernel selector will see different seq_len and pick a kernel that's suboptimal. Adding unit-tests around mask wrap should prevent regressions.

sanam: I'll push a PR with three commits: revert selector-branch (temporary), biased-modulo kv index, and mask wrap unit tests. Running A/B now across canary-3 and canary-4, will update perf numbers in ~20m.

alex: For the rollout plan: revert branch immediately to stop regressions, then land biased-modulo + mask-fix behind feature flag, run 24h canary, then flip selector branch re-enabled with the variance guard. :thumbsup:

maria: Also add an eval prompt set that exercises sliding-window at 6k-8k tokens so we catch this in nightlies.

sanam: Agreed. I'll attach a small repro and the microbench script to the PR. Thanks everyone.
